explanation: Overreach. The files show the app is built against 4.5.2 and App.config says supportedRuntime v4.0 with that sku; .NET Framework 4.x is an in-place update, so on a current Windows the program runs on the installed 4.8.x runtime, which is still supported. 'Gets no security fixes' and 'rebuilding on a supported runtime is needed' are not shown; what the lines show is an old target framework. Restate the risk at that reach (target is end-of-life; the runtime it executes on is whatever 4.x Windows has), lower or justify severity, keep externalSource for the 2022 date.

Cited lines show download then msiexec /a with no hash or signature check. 'The app may be running as administrator when it does so' is not shown by 84-91 and msiexec runs as the process user; say what admin changes (files re-ACLed at 60-71 and 96-98). The fixed predictable temp path under %localappdata% is omitted, and the same download is made with TLS 1.0 allowed (Main.vb:19-20), a weaker-transport detail the 'HTTPS is the only protection' claim should carry or get its own finding. Keep one risk but state its reach exactly.

The cited lines show only class declarations. 'Files are read straight into them', 'each dialog's entries are edited in its form controls' and 'no database or schema exists' are not shown by any cited line; cite the loaders (AdmxFile/AdmlFile/CmtxFile) and a dialog, or drop the clauses. State the headline rather than a list of type names.

'The only external address' is a claim across the code; support it by citing how the constant is used (DownloadAdmx.vb:84-91) and say no other URL or web call exists. The constant is pinned to a specific Windows 11 Sep 2026 (26H2) MSI and subdirectory (lines 3-4), so link and unpack path change with every Windows release: the decision-relevant point, missing. Language and ADMX folder are saved at Main.vb:60 and 478, not at the cited 23-29, which show only policy-source values.

The list leaves out user32 ShowScrollBar and SendNotifyMessageW (PInvoke.vb:3,13), so the stated purposes do not account for the change-notification broadcast; and a list of library names is something a person reads past. State the headline: Windows-only native calls for policy refresh, registry hive load/unload, privilege adjustment, plus the one external program msiexec (DownloadAdmx.vb:88-90).

The effective record dropped the workflow citation, so 'before the Release build' and 'no macros or build conditions beyond Debug and Release' are no longer shown by any cited line (vbproj conditions not cited). Restore .github/workflows/latest.yml:16-25 and cite the vbproj PropertyGroup conditions, or drop those clauses. Note the checked-in Version.vb holds an empty version string.

The effective record dropped what the earlier version had right. Line 9 shows the startup object is MyApplication, not that Main is the start form (Application.myapp:3-4 does). It also dropped the manifest's highestAvailable execution level (app.manifest:19), the main permission fact. Restore both; 'no role data exists' is unshown.

says: Nothing covers what the download dialog does to the file system as administrator: it enables SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilege, sets the owner of a user-typed destination folder to BUILTIN\Administrators, adds a FullControl rule, deletes any same-named file there and resets ACLs on moved files. The destination comes from a text box with no check that it is an ADMX folder. Give this its own risk finding citing these lines.

Weak transport setting: Main_Load enables Tls (1.0) and Tls11 alongside Tls12 for every web request, including the MSI download. No finding states this as a risk. Add one citing these lines, or fold into the MSI-download finding with the correct reach.

No fact covers how the program starts as a whole: the single start form, SingleInstance false, and the Main_Load sequence that opens the registry config, restores the ADMX folder and policy loaders and falls back to local GPO on failure. That start sequence is this technology's entry point.

Registry hive handling: OpenUserRegistry scans the hard-coded C:\Users and mounts other users' hives via RegLoadKeyW when running as administrator, and policy sources can be a user-chosen path. Loading a caller-given file path into the registry has no fact or finding; state its reach (administrator only, path from a dialog).
